title: Client-server and trust boundaries
caption: The browser reaches the proxy; the application performs authorized data access. Each hop has its own deadline and identity boundary.

title: ShopStream: modular monolith
caption: Modules share deployment and a local database transaction boundary. Payment is still a remote, independently failing dependency.

title: ShopStream: explicit service boundaries
caption: Separate services own data and communicate through contracts. This adds independent scaling and independent failure states.

title: Reverse proxy and backend selection
caption: The proxy selects a ready backend. Shared state and database capacity remain dependencies of both replicas.

title: Gateway policy and object authorization
caption: Gateway authentication and quota precede service-level ownership checks. A gateway pass is not blanket authorization.

title: Local and shared cache placement
caption: Local and shared caches reduce different costs. The source transaction and invalidation path determine freshness.

title: Durable queue and failure isolation
caption: Acknowledge only after the promised durable effect. Retry and DLQ paths remain visible instead of being counted as completion.

title: Independent subscription progress
caption: Each subscription has its own progress and failure handling. Consumers in one subscription can share work rather than each receiving every event.

title: Synchronous response and asynchronous completion
caption: Durable acceptance is an earlier milestone than business completion. A status API exposes the distinction.

title: Saga ownership and compensation
caption: The orchestrator persists progress and handles unknown outcomes. Compensation is a retryable business action, not time reversal.

title: Primary and asynchronously applied replicas
caption: Replica reads are selected by freshness requirements. Log transport and application can lag independently.

title: Shard routing and hot ownership
caption: The directory maps a key to an owner. Rebalancing must fence old ownership before stale routers can write divergent data.

title: Container image and host boundary
caption: The container shares the host kernel. Durable storage and network configuration are outside its disposable writable layer.

title: Kubernetes control and serving paths
caption: Controllers reconcile desired state; kubelets run workloads. Service eligibility depends on readiness and endpoint updates.

title: Immutable artifact promotion
caption: One artifact digest moves through environments. Configuration and migration compatibility are reviewed alongside the binary.

title: Correlated telemetry pipeline
caption: Metrics, logs, and traces retain different information. Shared operation and release IDs make evidence joinable.

title: Identity and resource authorization
caption: Login or delegated access establishes a principal. The final service still checks action and resource ownership.

title: Layered defensive application
caption: Filtering, authentication, authorization, safe query construction, and secret handling address different threats.

title: CDN edge and protected origin
caption: Nearby edges serve permitted copies. A miss converges on origin capacity, so cold-cache behavior needs its own test.

title: Multi-region authority and recovery
caption: A replica is not an independent writer until a safe authority transition occurs. Route availability and data consistency are separate decisions.

title: Backup, key access, and isolated restore
caption: Recovery needs both data and keys. Validation in isolation is evidence that the archived copy is actually usable.

title: Infrastructure plan and controlled apply
caption: Configuration, state, proposed changes, and live resources are distinct. Access to state and apply credentials is restricted.

title: Offline and online feature consistency
caption: Training and inference share a transformation contract but have different time and access requirements. Monitor materialization lag.

title: Serving reliability and model quality
caption: Operational success and useful predictions are evaluated independently, then combined in a release decision.

title: ShopStream production reference architecture
caption: Requests, durable state, asynchronous work, telemetry, and recovery are separate paths. Shared dependencies remain explicit.

title: HTTP request from name lookup to response
caption: Read top to bottom. Each arrow names a request or reply. Connection setup may be reused; a lost response does not prove a write failed.

title: Cache miss and bounded origin read
caption: A miss reaches the origin; a hit would return earlier. Concurrent refresh and update races require the policies in Topic 50.

title: Login and session creation
caption: Rotate session identifiers after authentication; cookies do not replace CSRF or object-level authorization.

title: Authorization code with PKCE
caption: The code is exchanged by the client. Validate redirect binding, issuer, and audience with maintained libraries.

title: Read after write with replica lag
caption: A session token or explicit primary route prevents a stale replica from falsely hiding a newly accepted order.

title: Deployment and health gates
caption: Startup gates other probes. Readiness controls routing eligibility; liveness has a separate restart purpose.

title: Trace context across synchronous and async work
caption: Async work may outlive the initial request. A trace link and operation ID preserve causality without pretending it is one synchronous stack.

title: Saga failure and compensating action
caption: Only a known payment decline takes this path. An unknown payment outcome first requires reconciliation; failed compensation remains durably pending.

title: Webhook delivery, retry, and durable acceptance
caption: A response can be lost after durable acceptance. Repeated delivery uses the same event identity and does not repeat the local effect.

title: Circuit breaker state transitions
caption: Closed records eligible outcomes. Open rejects calls. Half-open limits recovery probes; success closes and failure reopens.

title: Deployment lifecycle
caption: Rollback requires compatible data and configuration; an artifact change cannot undo irreversible effects.

title: Durable job lifecycle
caption: The result commits before acknowledgment. Retry waiting is durable in a real implementation; dead letter requires ownership.

title: Payment outcome and reconciliation
caption: Unknown is not declined. A refund is a new financial action, not erasure of the original payment.

title: Message processing lifecycle
caption: Redelivery can occur after the effect succeeded. Deduplicate at the effect boundary.

title: Incident lifecycle
caption: Recovery includes business integrity and queue freshness. Review produces owned verifiable actions.

title: Credential lifecycle
caption: Renewal requires its own valid grant. Expired or revoked access tokens must not authorize resource actions.

title: Cache entry lifecycle
caption: Expiration and eviction are different causes of absence. Refresh ownership limits a stampede.

title: How a good mean hides slow requests
caption: 980 fast and 20 slow requests yield a 59.6 ms mean but a 2000 ms P99. The bars are a schematic, not a scaled histogram.

title: Why a queue grows under sustained overload
caption: Arrival minus service gives the backlog growth rate. The continuous-time estimate differs slightly from the discrete tick convention in the runnable model.

title: Vertical and horizontal capacity
caption: A larger host and more hosts solve different constraints. Shared bottlenecks and failure domains still matter.

title: Copies versus divided ownership
caption: Top: each replica has A, B, and C. Bottom: shards own different subsets. Real systems can combine sharding with replication.

title: B-tree search narrows the candidate range
caption: The root directs key 72 toward the relevant sorted range. This is a conceptual tree; real page fanout and visibility rules are more complex.

title: One request, several latency budgets
caption: Add only sequential phases. Parallel work uses the critical path rather than the sum of every span.

title: From daily users to concurrent work
caption: Every step preserves its units and states its assumption. Peak factor and mean response time must later be measured.

title: Clock labels can contradict causal order
caption: The receiving host clock is behind. Use causal links for ordering and monotonic local clocks for elapsed time.

title: Exponential retry windows with full jitter
caption: Each retry samples a different window; the cap and total deadline still bound the policy.

title: Circuit breaker failure and recovery timeline
caption: Failures open the breaker, a cooldown rejects work, and a limited probe tests recovery. This timeline supplements the state diagram.

title: Recovery point and recovery time are different
caption: RPO concerns how recent recoverable data must be; RTO concerns how long restoring service may take.

title: Batching trades waiting for shared execution
caption: Bound both queue delay and memory. Compatible shapes and useful throughput determine whether batching helps.

title: Connection ownership and bounded waiting
caption: Each token represents one reusable connection. Exceptions must return ownership; adding application replicas multiplies potential demand.

title: Envelope encryption separates data and key protection
caption: The data key encrypts content; a separately controlled wrapping key protects the data key. Restore needs both authorized paths.

title: Fanout amplifies the probability of a slow branch
caption: The calculation assumes independent branch events and all branches required. Correlation and partial-result contracts change the result.

title: Expand-and-contract migration sequence
caption: The old contract remains during mixed-version operation. Removing it is a separate, later change after backfill and rollback requirements are satisfied.

title: Backpressure as a bounded restaurant ticket rack
caption: Left: arriving orders accumulate faster than one chef can finish them. Right: the same chef has a bounded rack and upstream admission pauses. The illustration is qualitative; the queue model supplies the arithmetic.
